heard: Physicists found a hidden dead star a million times faster. Standard methods burned 600 years of computing and found nothing. NASA's Fermi telescope captures only sparse photons across the sky. Sifting through noise used to swallow whole volunteer computing networks. So, researchers borrowed math designed to test quantum encryption. They mapped the search as geometry in a high-dimensional lattice. A standard computer processor found the target in 10 hours. It revealed a pulsar spinning 261 times per second. No telescope search had ever moved so fast.
